model_annotation: Figure 4 displays a bar chart illustrating the number of participants (N = 6) who highlighted each evaluation criterion as beneficial. The horizontal axis lists the evaluation criteria, presented in the order: “retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs)”, “concise summaries”, “explanations”, and “clarity of the interface”. The vertical axis represents the count of participants, scaled linearly from 0 to 6, with tick marks at intervals of 1. Each criterion is represented by a single, solid blue bar. The bar for “retrieval of relevant fact-checks (FCs)” is the tallest, reaching a value of 6, indicating all six participants found it beneficial. The bars for “concise summaries”, “explanations”, and “clarity of the interface” are all of equal height, each reaching a value of 3, indicating that three participants found each of these criteria beneficial. The bars are arranged in descending order of participant count, with the tallest bar on the left and the shortest bars on the right. There is no visual emphasis, such as shading or outlining, applied to any of the bars.
